newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU delays approval of wheat export tax.
newsitem.headline: EU delays approval of wheat export tax.

text.p: The European Commission delayed approval of a European Union tax on daily soft wheat grain and flour exports, a European Commission official said on Wednesday.
"Someone has asked for a more detailed explanation," the official said, declining further details. The official was unable to say when the tax might now be adopted and enter into force.
However, EU sources said France was opposed to proposed taxes of 15 Ecus a tonne on daily exports of soft wheat grain and 20 Ecus a tonne on wheat flour.

The proposal was due to have been adopted without discussion on Wednesday under the EU's so-called written procedure. Exporters who have taken out a nil value export licence will be liable to tax if they have not customs cleared their grain and flour exports before the tax is approved.
On April 24, the EU cereals management committee, made up of delegates from member states, supported the move which is aimed at saving supplies for domestic consumers and dampening prices.
Concern over world crop prospects following frost in the United States and a long spell of dry weather in Europe had driven prices some 20 percent above EU intervention levels.
On April 17, the EU closed a weekly tender for this season's wheat exports, several weeks earlier than usual.

The EU started 1996/97 with a wheat export tax when stocks were low and prices high but restored export refunds in September when prospects of bumper crops in the main producer countries dampened world prices.
